rationale.complete: Round 1 done: dated predictions plus three disclosed amendments; synthetic validation on the real call schedules (6 worlds x 2 base rates x 20 runs, frozen decision rule); 30 period folders (23 replication incl. 4 native tests, 7 descriptive) with predictions written before each run; scorecard; operator rules; confirm.py frozen and dry-run on stand-ins. Holdout not run; deadline-bound calls tested only in #26.
rationale.faithfulness: The core claim (wave size set by the receptive fraction at the call-cycle scale) is refuted: RR_timely 1.06 [0.93, 1.22], R adds nothing out of sample, current share wins. Card rule: failed. The announcement-seeded part holds at a descriptive level (step at the link, room-bounded, read-out gated), and the #26 runoff shows wave = receptive count for a deadline-bound call. Scorecard A1 B1 C0 D1 E1 F1 G1 H0 I0.
rationale.usefulness: Two operator rules with evidence: announce projects (a first link seeds a ~20x wave; timing to the call clock adds <=9%), and for votes/polls size the window to read-out delays (a 2-min window disenfranchises ~1/3 of a regime-III swarm; >=15 min reaches ~90%). Calibrated 2.0 -> 2.5.

one_line: Herding is announcement-seeded (adoptions jump ~20x at a project's first chat link and stay in the poster's room), but the call clock doesn't set wave size: prompt readers adopt no more (RR 1.06), and current share, not the receptive count, predicts pile-ons. The clock binds only for deadline-bound calls (#26 runoff: ballots = readers in window).
